videos.title: Most Microsoft Fabric Workspaces Are Organized Wrong
videos.description:
Most teams treat **Microsoft Fabric workspaces like folders**.

A place to organize reports.
A place to store dashboards.
A place to group projects.

But workspaces aren’t folders.

They define **accountability boundaries**.

In this video, Patrick walks through how he evaluates *workspace structure in Microsoft Fabric* and why poor workspace design leads to:

• unclear ownership
• project sprawl
• permission chaos
• blurred Dev vs Test vs Prod boundaries

Using a real Fabric environment, Patrick explores:

• Why project-based workspaces create long-term problems
• How to identify *domain ownership boundaries*
• Why *environment separation (Dev / Test / Prod)* matters
• How workspace permissions reveal responsibility
• What a *Domain × Environment* structure looks like in practice

If you watched Marthe’s video on **Domains in Microsoft Fabric**, she covers the feature itself and how it fits into governance.

This video takes a step back and looks at *domains as an architectural boundary* — whether you’re using the feature or not.

This is part of a larger series on **Responsibility-First Architecture**, where the stack is explored from:

Capacity → Workspace → Data Platform → Semantic Model

If you're working with **Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, or modern data platforms**, this perspective helps you think beyond tools and focus on **structure, ownership, and accountability**.
